title: Longest Stretch Where Every Letter Shows k Times
statement:
You get a lowercase string s and an integer k.

Find the longest contiguous substring in which every letter that appears in it appears at least k times. Return its length, or 0 if no non-empty substring qualifies.

examples.why: "c" appears once in the whole string, so no answer can contain it. Left of it, "abba" has two a's and two b's. Right of it, "ab" fails.
The whole string has three m's, but the n's sit between them. Every substring holding all three m's also holds an n, which appears only twice.
"tttuu" works. Adding the final "t" would need crossing the lone "v".

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
hints: If a letter appears fewer than k times in the whole string, can any valid substring contain it?
No. So such a letter splits the string into pieces, and the answer lives inside one of them. Recurse on each piece.
For a linear-style alternative: fix the number of distinct letters u from 1 to 26 and run a sliding window that keeps exactly u distinct letters, tracking how many of them already reach k.

explain.intuition:
A plain sliding window does not work directly: adding a letter can make a window invalid, and adding a few more of that letter can make it valid again. The window has no single direction to move.

The fix is to look at letters that are too rare. If some letter appears fewer than k times in the current string, no valid substring can include it, so it acts as a wall. Split the string at every such wall and solve each piece on its own. If no letter is too rare, the whole piece is valid. Each split removes at least one letter from the pieces below it, so the recursion is at most 26 levels deep.
steps: Write solve(lo, hi) for the substring s[lo..hi). Count its letters.
If every letter that appears has count ≥ k, return hi − lo.
Otherwise walk through the range. Positions holding a letter with count < k are walls; call solve on each stretch between walls.
Return the largest result. The answer is solve(0, n).
pitfalls: Checking only that each letter of the whole string appears k times, without making the substring contiguous. In "mmnmn" the m's are not together.
Splitting at just the first rare letter and keeping the rest. Every rare letter is a wall, and pieces must be recounted because their counts are smaller than the parent's.
Growing a sliding window and shrinking whenever a letter is below k. A letter below k may still reach k later, so that shrink throws away valid answers.

complexity.space: O(26) per level, at most 26 levels

solutions.title: Every start, extend with counts
solutions.idea: For each start, extend the end one letter at a time, keeping counts and the number of letters still below k.

solutions.title: Split at letters that are too rare
solutions.idea: A letter seen fewer than k times in the range can never be part of the answer, so it splits the range into independent pieces.

solutions.title: Sliding window per number of distinct letters
solutions.idea: Fix u, the exact number of distinct letters allowed. Now the window has a direction: shrink when it holds more than u. Count windows where all u letters reach k.

followups: Why does the plain sliding window fail here, and what exactly does fixing the number of distinct letters restore?
Return the substring itself, choosing the leftmost one on ties.
lcTitle: Longest Substring with At Least K Repeating Characters
